chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek supplication during four timings: at the gusting of the winds, the decline of the shadows, the descent of the rain, and the first drop of blood of the murdered believer, for the doors of the sky are opened at these things.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four best times for supplication according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies four specific natural and spiritual moments when supplication is particularly likely to be accepted: the gusting of winds, the shortening of shadows, the falling of rain, and the first drop of blood from a martyred believer. These times are described as moments when the doors of heaven are opened. In Shia tradition, these moments are viewed as times of heightened cosmic receptivity, where the veil between the earthly and divine realms thins, allowing for a more direct connection with the Divine Will.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from Zayd Al Shahaam who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Seek the supplication during four timings – during the gusts of the winds, and the decline of the shadows, and the descent of the (rain) drops, and the first drop of blood of the murdered Momin, for the doors of the sky are Opened during these things’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn abu al-Belad from his father from Ziyad al- Shahham who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Seek prayer in four hours: at the time of the blowing of winds, at the time of vanishing of shadows, at the time of the coming of raindrops and at the time the first drop of the blood of a believing person murdered spills. At such times the doors of the heavens open up.’”
